clue.text: Crazy single issue president

parts.note: crazy means mad
I is the Roman numeral one, a single
issue means offspring, so a son

explanation.surface: A mad one-issue politician running for the White House.
explanation.definitionFit: James Madison was the fourth President of the United States.

clue.text: Musical doctor — see within

indicators.note: within says the second word goes inside the doctor

parts.note: a medic is a doctor
lo is an old word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: A doctor who plays music; take a look inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Melodic means tuneful, having melody, so musical.

clue.text: Wait carefully: take to the floor at 2200 hrs — again

parts.note: to take to the floor is to dance
2200 hours is ten o'clock at night
again says the dancing word is repeated

explanation.surface: Instructions for an evening of ballroom dancing at ten.
explanation.definitionFit: To dance attendance is to wait on someone obsequiously, attending to every need.

clue.text: Childless woman in charge almost all round

parts.note: s.p., sine prole, is genealogical shorthand for without issue
her stands for a woman

indicators.note: almost says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written before it is cut

explanation.surface: A woman with no children who is nearly in charge of everything.
explanation.walkthrough: SP, Latin sine prole (without offspring), is used in family trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Spherical means shaped like a ball, perfectly round.

clue.text: Setter laments rise of Biblical widow

indicators.note: in a down clue rise says the phrase is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the setter says I moan

explanation.surface: A crossword setter grumbling about a widow from the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi, mother-in-law of Ruth, was widowed in Moab in the Book of Ruth.

clue.text: Far-reaching reduction in military establishment

definitions.meaning: A British Army barracks in Surrey

explanation.surface: Swingeing cuts to a military base.
explanation.definitionFit: A drastic cutback is called deep, and Deepcut is the name of an army barracks in Surrey, England.

clue.text: A spy spied — hence that uncomfortable feeling?

indicators.note: hence says what follows arises out of these letters, worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A spy who has been spotted gets an unsettled stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyspepsia is indigestion, an uncomfortable feeling in the stomach.

clue.text: Uniform as in railway

indicators.note: in says the Latin word goes inside the railway

parts.note: EL is the elevated railway, as in Chicago
qua is Latin for in the capacity of, as

explanation.surface: Railway uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Equal can mean even or uniform, the same throughout.

clue.text: Can't gas children, possibly, but could be abducting them

indicators.note: possibly says these letters may be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A grim line about gassing children, swerving into kidnapping.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken literally, snatching babies from cradles is abducting children; the everyday sense is dating a much younger partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking babies out of their cradles would literally be abducting children.

clue.text: Hear those that see; they have it in passing

indicators.note: hear signals a word said aloud that sounds like the entered letters

parts.note: the organs that see are the eyes

explanation.surface: A sound check on whether people with sight have something.
explanation.walkthrough: In Parliament the Speaker announces 'the ayes have it' when a motion is passed.
explanation.definitionFit: The yes voters, who carry the day when a bill is passed.

clue.text: Salami for the one French revolutionary discussing some of its treatment

indicators.note: the salami's sausage stands in after the other pieces, so the order here is set by the answer

parts.note: in French 'the one' is l'un
Che Guevara is the crossword's standard revolutionary
on means about, discussing
salami is a kind of sausage

explanation.surface: A French revolutionary holding forth about how salami should be treated.
explanation.walkthrough: The sausage from 'Salami' goes at the end. The definition is loose in Araucaria's way: salami gets cut into slices, as does this cheap processed meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Luncheon sausage is a sliced processed meat, the same handling a salami receives.

clue.text: Gloomy otologist?

definitions.meaning: an ear specialist could jokingly be called Doctor Ear

explanation.surface: A depressed ear specialist.
explanation.definitionFit: Drear is a literary form of dreary, meaning dismal or gloomy.

clue.text: Diamonds twice the money with stick inserted?

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds
two words for money: D, the old penny
lolly is British slang for money

explanation.surface: Diamonds costing double, with a stick pushed in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice the money' gives two money words: D (the old British penny) and LOLLY (slang for cash). An ICED LOLLY is the British name for an ice pop on a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A frozen treat on a stick: the stick is inserted before freezing, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Burial places for Manx cat: put another one back in them

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the word cat loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written before its tail goes

indicators.note: in says the turned cat goes inside the word for the burial places

parts.note: them refers back to the burial places, tombs

indicators.note: back says this second tailless cat is read in the other direction

parts.note: another Manx cat, so again CA

explanation.surface: Instructions for burying tailless cats with a second one alongside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'them' stands for the burial places, TOMBS; 'put another one back in them' puts AC (CA turned round) inside, giving TACOMBS after the first CA.
explanation.definitionFit: Catacombs are underground cemeteries with galleries of tombs.

clue.text: Being drugged, perhaps, got married without decree (not absolute)

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the marriage word goes round the decree

parts.note: mated means paired off, married

indicators.note: not absolute says the decree is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: an edict is a decree

explanation.surface: Divorce talk: married, but no decree absolute yet.
explanation.walkthrough: A decree absolute is the final order in an English divorce; here 'not absolute' trims the decree.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicated means treated with drugs, as a patient being dosed might be.

clue.text: Zoroastrians with no leader — that's where the stress comes

indicators.note: no leader says the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: Parsis are Zoroastrians of Indian descent

explanation.surface: A leaderless religious group where stress builds up.
explanation.definitionFit: In prosody the arsis is the accented, stressed part of a metrical foot.

clue.text: Bear North? Hardly, it's far from desirable

indicators.note: hardly in the sense of harshly, roughly, so these letters are treated roughly into a new order

explanation.surface: A polar bear heading north is hardly a welcome sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Abhorrent means loathsome, the very opposite of desirable.

clue.text: Live and die initially successfully

indicators.note: initially says take the first letter of die

parts.note: doing something successfully is doing it well

explanation.surface: Advice on how to live and die well.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to live or reside there.

clue.text: Pleasure obtained from French fast mover

parts.note: de is French for from
light travels faster than anything else

explanation.surface: Pleasure from a speedy French vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Delight is great pleasure.

clue.text: Paid back the Queen about a paper disc

indicators.note: back says the word paid is read in the other direction

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned

indicators.note: about says the royal letters go round the paper

parts.note: HM is Her Majesty
rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A refund handed back to the Queen over a paper disc.
explanation.definitionFit: A diaphragm is a disc-shaped part, such as a contraceptive cap or a vibrating membrane.

clue.text: People about to travel in Middle England

indicators.note: about says the people go round the travelling word

parts.note: men means people
to ride is to travel

explanation.surface: People travelling across the English heartland.
explanation.walkthrough: MERIDEN is a village near Coventry long claimed as the centre of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Meriden is traditionally held to be the central point of England.

clue.text: She's a living member of a cathedral choir without note

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the singer's title goes round the note

parts.note: a lay vicar is a lay singer in a cathedral choir
D is a musical note

explanation.surface: A singing member of a cathedral choir who can't hit a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking. A living is a church benefice, held by a vicar.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman priest holding a parish benefice, which the Church calls a living.

clue.text: Letter sent with love

indicators.note: sent in the sense of sent off or transported, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A letter posted with love.
explanation.definitionFit: A vowel is a letter such as A, E, I, O or U.

clue.text: Proportion in preparation

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the word preparation

explanation.surface: Getting the proportions right in preparation.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio is a proportion between two quantities.

clue.text: Note on incomplete remedy will not be for the first time

definitions.text: will not be for the first time

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: incomplete says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a cure is a remedy

explanation.surface: A half-finished remedy that won't work at the first attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that recurs happens again, so its coming is not a first occurrence.

clue.text: Mitchell's set sail without having to tack

definitions.meaning: Margaret Mitchell wrote one famous novel, so hers is her book

definitions.text: set sail without having to tack
definitions.meaning: a ship sailing downwind need not tack

explanation.surface: Someone sets sail and finds no need to zigzag against the breeze.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1936 novel by Margaret Mitchell, and literally a description of sailing downwind.

clue.text: High note, high note, high note

definitions.text: High note, high note, high note

parts.words: High note, high note, high note
parts.note: a high note is a treble, and saying it three times makes it threefold

explanation.surface: A singer hitting the top note again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: Trebled means tripled, and the clue gives a treble three times over.

clue.text: Figure of 100 in part of New Zealand (North)

indicators.note: in says the hundred goes inside the New Zealand region

parts.note: Otago is a region of New Zealand's South Island
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A population figure of a hundred in a corner of New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: An octagon is an eight-sided plane figure.
